verdicts.quote: “To access the Apify API in your integrations, you need to authenticate using your secret API token.”
verdicts.reason: Docs specify personal API tokens passed via Authorization/Bearer, matching Bearer/PAT token. ([docs.apify.com](https://docs.apify.com/integrations/api))

verdicts.quote: “The free plan includes monthly platform usage credits with no credit card required.”
verdicts.reason: Free signup yields usage credits; same page shows how to create an API token in Console, so credentials are self‑serve. ([docs.apify.com](https://docs.apify.com/agents/quickstart))

verdicts.quote: “All aspects of the Apify platform can be controlled via a REST API, which is described in detail in the API Reference.”
verdicts.reason: API reference covers Actors, Versions, Runs, Storage (datasets, key‑value stores, request queues), Webhooks, Schedules, Users, Logs, etc., indicating breadth. ([docs.apify.com](https://docs.apify.com/integrations/api))

verdicts.quote: “The Apify's MCP server (mcp.apify.com) allows AI applications and agents to interact with the Apify platform using Model Context Protocol (MCP).”
verdicts.reason: Vendor‑hosted MCP at mcp.apify.com; page also documents OAuth or bearer token auth and a local stdio server option. ([docs.apify.com](https://docs.apify.com/mcp))

verdicts.quote: “You manage your tokens on the API & Integrations page in Apify Console.”
verdicts.reason: Self‑serve tokens plus comprehensive REST API and no app‑review/partner gating mean Composio could ship now. ([docs.apify.com](https://docs.apify.com/integrations/api))
